title: Copeces
summary: Copeces is an Indigenous place name connected with a locality at the head of Three Mile Harbor in East Hampton. It is associated with Hand's Creek and the sheltered inner harbor area near Ashawagh.
address_label: Hand's Creek / head of Three Mile Harbor, East Hampton, NY (approximate general location)
map_geometry_source: Copeces is placed at the head of Three Mile Harbor. The point uses a modern approximate/general Hand's Creek launch/location reference and is not an exact historic boundary.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Copeces and Copecs. The name is interpreted as a little shut-in or sheltered place, connecting it with related forms such as Copiag and Copwax.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are used to identify key landmarks and features in our environment and represent cultural values. They have long-term impacts on a person’s sense of identity and belonging.”

— Queensland Department of Natural Resources and Mines, Manufacturing and Regional and Rural Development, Naming places in Queensland (2024), opening text
land_loss_content: Copeces preserves a creek and harbor name tied to Montaukett use of sheltered waters, meadow, shellfish, and travel around Three Mile Harbor. Recording it separately from Ashawagh keeps the water-place name visible without separating it from the related settlement landscape.
whereintheworld_content: William Wallace Tooker associates Copeces with Hand's Creek near the head of Three Mile Harbor. The precise historic locality remains uncertain.
